subject: Question about different # of visits per site using occu

messages.author: ff8b92e3478bd700
messages.subject: Question about different # of visits per site using occu
parts:
Hi,

I have a one season/year data set with 160 sites. Of the 160 sites - 60 were visited 3 times and 100 were visited 2 times. I have 6 site covariates for each site (% cover variables) and 2 observation covariates (date and time). I am using occu to measure probability of detection and occupancy for an individual specie.
Can I group the data set together and run the analysis even though the 3rd visits will be NA for 100 sites or should I analyze the data separately so sites have equal number of visits?(e.g., Analysis 1: sites with 3 visits and Analysis 2: sites with 2 visits (getting prob of detection and occupancy for both scenarios)) 

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Question about different # of visits per site using occu
parts:
Dear Nicole,

the data set for an occupancy analysis does not need to be balanced. In fact, I have almost never seen a data set for an occupancy model that was strictly balanced, i.e., had the same replication everywhere.

So, one single analysis is fine.

Kind regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Question about different # of visits per site using occu
parts:
Dear Nicole,

if the single-visit sites are a random subset from all sites, then no problem with them.

The only problem is when they are "different", for instance, less "good" sites, where population density of the critters is lower, and so people didn't want to pay a large effort at such sites where they are less likely to see things.

If this latter was true, then p would be greater in the sites with replication, which provide (almost) all info about p, and the estimate of p would be biased high and that for psi biased low.

Kind regards --  Marc
